title: County differences in curative-intent treatment are far larger than chance
finding_en: If every county treated at the national rate of 27.0%, chance alone would put about one county outside the 95% limits. Twelve of 22 are outside. Lapland, South Karelia and Kymenlaakso are below even the 99.8% limits. The seven counties below the limits are together about 50 patients a year short of the national share. When the limits are widened to allow for how much counties differ from each other anyway, only Lapland and Helsinki stay outside. This is not adjusted for stage or age, because those are not published per county, so it shows where to look, not why.
figure_alt: Funnel plot: share of lung cancer patients who received curative-intent treatment against the number of patients, one point per county, with control limits around the national 27.0%. Twelve counties are labelled outside the limits.
